description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs:849-1248 (handle_filenode_copy, parent-id-override path).

When `fromAccountId == accountId` (in-account copy, which RFC 8620
§5.4 explicitly allows), the FileNode/copy handler reads a source
node, optionally overrides `parentId` via the copy descriptor at
lines 968-984, and then calls `create_object` with the (potentially
new-parent) clone. There is NO cycle check.

Trigger: a user copies directory `dirA` (which contains a subtree
`dirA → dirB → dirC`) and supplies `parentId: "dirC"` in the copy
descriptor. The handler:

1. Fetches `dirA` from the source.
2. Applies the override: source_node.parent_id = Some(Id("dirC")).
3. Calls find_sibling_by_name in destination, finds no collision.
4. Calls create_object, which inserts dirA-copy under dirC.

Result: a new node dirA-copy exists with parentId=dirC. Because
dirC was a descendant of dirA, the resulting in-account tree has
a forest-with-cycle property: walking parent links from dirA-copy
gets dirC → dirB → dirA (the ORIGINAL dirA, not dirA-copy), so
strictly there is no cycle on the new node — BUT subsequent
mutations that try to move dirA under dirA-copy WOULD create one,
and any iteration that mixes source nodes and copies will be
surprising.

A stronger trigger: same as above but with onSuccessDestroyOriginal=true
(which the handler ignores per bd:JMAP-510h.56, but assume that is
fixed). Then dirA itself is destroyed AFTER the copy, and the
destroy fails because dirA has children (dirB) that were not in the
destroy set. The user sees a partial-success state: dirA-copy now
exists under dirC, dirA still exists. The tree structure is
inconsistent with the user's intent.

Compare handle_filenode_set's update path (filenode.rs:580-627):
it calls `get_descendant_ids(id)` and rejects if the proposed new
parent is in the descendant set. The same check is missing on
copy when the source account == destination account.

Required fix:

1. When fromAccountId == accountId AND the copy descriptor includes
   a parentId override, fetch the descendants of the source node
   via `get_descendant_ids(caller, &from_account_id, &source_id)`.
2. If the proposed new parent is in the descendant set, place the
   entry in `notCreated` with `invalidProperties: ["parentId"]`
   and description "copying this node under its own descendant
   would create a cycle".
3. Document the same-account-copy semantics in the handler doc
   comment so consumers know the guard exists.

This is `defensive` rather than `bug` because the cycle is not
strictly created — a fresh node is created — but the semantic
intent of the user (a copy that mirrors the source as a subtree)
is silently violated.

LABELS: api-contract, defensive, spec
title: handle_filenode_copy with fromAccountId == accountId can create a cycle (copy a directory under itself)
